source_text:
ἐπισπάσηται· οὐ γὰρ τοῖς ἐν μηδενὶ συμφωνοῦσι συντίθενται ποσῶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι,
ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐκ μέρους αὐτοῖς συντιθεμένοις. 1 Kor 9,23Ἐπειδὴ καὶ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ δοκεῖ
μὴ κεχρῆσθαι νόμῳ, ἐμιμησάμην αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκονομίαν, ὅπερ ἐκεῖνο βούλεται
οἰκονομῶν, ἵνα κατ' αὐτὸ τοῦτο αὐτῷ κοινωνήσω.Ἐπειδὴ καὶ τῷ εὐαγγελικῷ δοκεῖ
χρῆσθαι νόμῳ, ἐμιμησάμην αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκονομίαν· ὅπερ γὰρ ἐκεῖνο εἶπεν, τοῦτο
οἰκονομῶ. 1 Kor 9,24 Οὐ τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ἡμῶν πάντων προκρίνεται–ἢ γὰρ ἂν
καὶ ἀπέγνωσαν ἑαυτῶν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἰς τὸ δυσκατόρθωτον ἀποβλέποντες–ἀλλὰ
δηλονότι ἡ εἰκὼν πρὸς τὰ εἰρημένα αὐτῷ ἔθνη εἴληπται. πάντες, φησίν, ὡς ἐν
σταδίῳ τῷ βίῳ τούτῳ ἀγωνίζονται,Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν κατὰ νόμον,Ἕλληνες δὲ κατὰ
πλάνην, εἷς δέ ἐστιν ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγος, ὁ νικῶν καὶ λαμβάνων τὸ βραβεῖον. διὸ
τρέχετε ἵνα μὴ σὺν τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀπολειφθῆτε. 1 Kor 9,25 Τί μέγα, φησίν, ἐὰν
ἐγκρατεύσησθε σαρκὶ διὰ τὸν ἀδελφόν; πάντα δεῖ ἐγκρατεύεσθαι τὸν ἀγωνιζόμενον,
ἀπὸ θυμοῦ, ἀπὸ δόξης καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν λοιπῶν· ἐκεῖνοι μὲν οὖν ἵνα φθαρτὸν
στέφανον λάβωσιν, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄφθαρτον. Τοῦτο οὐχ ἁπλῶς εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ διορθούμενος
τοὺς ἕνεκεν τοῦ 258 γαστρίζεσθαι φιλοσοφεῖν προσποιουμένους, ὅτι τὸ εἰδωλόθυτον
οὐκ ἔστιν εἰδωλόθυτον. 257,ξολ2 Οὐχ ἁπλῶς τοῦτο εἶπεν ἀλλὰ διορθούμενος τοὺς
ἕνεκεν τοῦ 258,ξολ2 γαστρίζεσθαι ἀδιαφόρως ἐσθίειν τὰ ἱερόθυτα ἐν πίστει
προσποιουμένους. 1 Kor 10,1–8 Τοὺς ἐκ τῆς παλαιᾶς τύπους καὶ τὰς ἐκεῖθεν σκιὰς
προεικονιζούσας τὴν μέλλουσαν ἀλήθειαν εἰς μέσον ἄγει ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, ἵνα
σωφρονίσῃ τοὺς Korινθίους ἐκ τῆς τῶν παλαιῶν παραθέσεως. εἰ γάρ φησιν· οἱ εἰς
τὸν Μωϋσῆν βαπτισθέντες, ὃς ἦν τύπος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ τῇ θαλάσσῃ
καὶ φαγόντες τὸ μάννα, τὸ πνευματικὸν βρῶμα, καὶ πιόντες ἐκ τῆς πέτρας τὸ
πνευματικὸν πόμα κατεστρώθησαν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, εἰς μέθας καὶ πορνείας καὶ
εἰδωλολατρείας τραπέντες, ὅτι τὸν τύπον καὶ τὴν σκιὰν ὕβρισαν, τί οὐκ ἂν πάθοιεν
οἱ εἰς αὐτὴν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἁμαρτάνοντες; 1 Kor 10,9Ἐπειδὴ ἔλεγον· ἐμοὶ εἴδωλον
οὐκ ἔστιν· εὐχαριστῶ γὰρ καὶ ἐσθίω, τοῦτο, φησίν, ἐκπειράσαι ἐστίν. ὃ γὰρ μὴ
προσέταξενἸησοῦς ὅταν ὡς πιστεύων αὐτῷ ποιῇς, ἐκπειράζεις μᾶλλον ἢ πιστεύεις.
Τοῦτο φησι πρὸς τοὺς λέγοντας· ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν εἴδωλόν ἐστιν· εὐχαριστῶ γὰρ καὶ ἐσθίω,
ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἐκπειράζειν. ἃ γὰρ μὴ προσέταξεν ὁ κύριος ὅταν ὡς πιστεύων αὐτῷ ποιῇς,
ἐκπειράζεις μᾶλλον ἢ πιστεύεις. 1 Kor 10,11 Εἰς ὑμᾶς, φησί, κατήντησεν ἡ τοῦ
Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημία, μεθ' ἣν οὐκέτι ἔσται οὐκ ἐντολὴ οὐ νόμος οὐ προφῆται· τέλη γὰρ
λέγει οὐ τὴν ἐσχάτην γενεὰν καθ' ἣν συμπλήρωσις ἔσται τοῦ κόσμου, ἀλλὰ τὴν
τελευταίαν πολιτείαν τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ ἐφ' ᾗ τῶν αἰώνων ἡ συμπλήρωσις ἀπαντήσει. 1
Kor 10,13 Οὐκ ηὔξατο μὴ πειρασθῆναι, ἐπειδὴ ἀνὴρ ἀπείραστος ἀδόκιμος, ἀλλ'
οὕτως πειράζεσθαι ὡς φέρειν. Ἐκ τούτου δηλοῖ ὅτι ὑπέμεινάν τινας ἀηδίας ἐκ τῶν
πολιτῶν οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς πιστεύσαντες. εἶτα οὐκ ηὔξατο αὐτοὺς μὴ πειρασθῆναι, ἐπειδὴ
ἀνὴρ ἀπείραστος ἀδόκιμος, ἀλλ' οὕτω πειρασθῆναι ὡς φέρειν. 259 1 Kor 10,14 Ὁρᾷς
ὅτι πάντα τὰ προειρημένα αὐτῷ τούτου ἕνεκα κατεσκευάζετο. Ἦλθεν ἐφ' ᾧ
κατεσκεύαζεν· πάντα γὰρ ὅσα προεῖπεν πρὸς τὸ ἀποστῆσαι αὐτοὺς τῆς
εἰδωλολατρείας ἐλέγετο καὶ κατεσκευάζετο. 1 Kor 10, Μὴ πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα αὐτῶν
ἀποβλέπετε οὐδὲν ὄντα, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὴν διάνοιαν καθ' ἣν θύουσι δαιμονίοις καὶ οὐ
θεῷ· τὸ γὰρ γινόμενον ὥσπερ εἰς ἄρνησιν γίνεται τοῦ θεοῦ. 1 Kor 10,22 Ἐπειδὴ
γέγραπται ὁ θεὸς λέγων διὰ Μωϋσέως αὐτοῖς· παρεζήλωσάν με ἐπ' οὐ θεοῖς,
παρώργισάν με ἐν τοῖς εἰδώλοις αὐτῶν, οἱ δὲ Korίνθιοι εἰδωλόθυτα ἤσθιον, διὰ
τοῦτό φησιν· ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον;–ἀντὶ τοῦ παροξύνομεν αὐτόν; –μὴ
ἰσχυρότεροι αὐτοῦ ἔσμεν; ἔδειξε διὰ τούτου, ὅτι οὐ θέλει ὁ κύριος εἰδωλόθυτα ἡμᾶς
ἐσθίειν. μὴ τοίνυν, φησί, θέλε ἃ μὴ θέλει ὁ κύριος, ὡς ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ καὶ
συνετώτερος. Ἢ εἰς ζῆλον αὐτὸν κινοῦμεν καὶ παροξύνομεν; εἴρηται γὰρ παρὰ
Μωϋσεῖ· αὐτοὶ παρεζήλωσάν με ἐπ' οὐ θεοῖς, παρώργισάν με ἐν τοῖς εἰδώλοις αὐτῶν.
ταῦτα δέ φησιν, ἐπειδὴ εἰδωλόθυτα οἱ Korίνθιοι ἤσθιον. 1 Kor 10,25 Ἐπειδὴ εἰκὸς ἦν
αὐτοὺς ἀκριβολογουμένους μηκέτι τολμᾶν μήτε ὀψωνεῖν φόβῳ τοῦ μὴ ἀκοῦσαι
«εἰδωλόθυτον ἠγόρασας», παραμυθεῖται τὸν φόβον. συνείδησιν δὲ λέγει οὐ τὴν τοῦ
ἐγνωκότος ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον, ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ ἑωρακότος τὸν ἀγοράζοντα τὸ
pass_a_gloss: [9:22 note, continued] ...he may draw over [them] to himself; for people do not at all come to terms with those who agree with them in nothing, but with those who agree with them in part. [Label 1 Kor 9,23] Since to the gospel too it seems not to have used law, I imitated its management, managing what that one wishes, so that in this very thing I may share with it. [Second form, not printed again: Since to the gospel-[law] too it seems to use law, I imitated its management; for what that one said, this I manage.] [Label 1 Kor 9,24] He does not say this, that one out of us all is preferred (or else people would have despaired of themselves, looking at the difficulty of success), but clearly the image has been taken toward the nations mentioned by him. All, he says, compete in this life as in a stadium, Jews according to law, Greeks according to error, but one is the word of truth, the one winning and taking the prize. Therefore run, so that you may not be left behind with the others. [Label 1 Kor 9,25] What great thing, he says, if you control yourselves in meat because of the brother? The one competing must control himself in all things: from anger, from glory, and from all the rest; they then, so that they may take a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one. He did not say this simply, but correcting those who for the sake of filling the belly pretend to philosophize that idol-sacrifice is not idol-sacrifice. [Second form, 257 col2, not printed again: He did not say this simply but correcting those who for the sake of filling the belly pretend to eat the temple-sacrifices indifferently, in faith.] [Label 1 Kor 10,1-8] The divine Paul brings into the middle the types from the old [covenant] and the shadows from there that prefigured the coming truth, so that he may make the Corinthians prudent from the comparison with the ancients. For if, he says, those baptized into Moses (who was a type of Christ) in the cloud and the sea, and having eaten the manna, the spiritual food, and having drunk from the rock the spiritual drink, were laid low in the desert, having turned to drunkenness and fornications and idolatries, because they insulted the type and the shadow, what would those not suffer who sin against the truth itself? [Label 1 Kor 10,9] Since they said: for me there is no idol, for I give thanks and eat, this, he says, is to put to the test. For what Jesus did not command, when you do it as trusting him, you test rather than trust. [Second form, not printed again: He says this to those saying: for me no idol is anything, for I give thanks and eat, which is to put to the test; for what the Lord did not command, when you do it as trusting him, you test rather than trust.] [Label 1 Kor 10,11] To you, he says, the coming of Christ has arrived, after which there will be no longer commandment, not law, not prophets; for he says 'ends' not [meaning] the last generation according to which there will be a completion of the world, but the final way of life, the one in Christ, upon which the completion of the ages will arrive. [Label 1 Kor 10,13] He did not pray [for them] not to be tested, since an untested man is unproven, but to be tested so as to bear it. [Second form] From this he shows that those who believed among them endured some unpleasantnesses from the citizens. [Not printed again: Then he did not pray for them not to be tested, since an untested man is unproven, but to be tested so as to bear it.] [Label 1 Kor 10,14] You see that all the things said before by him were prepared for the sake of this. [Second form, not printed again: He came to what he was preparing; for all things he said before were said and prepared toward separating them from idolatry.] [Label 1 Kor 10, (verse missing)] Do not look toward their idols, being nothing, but toward the intention according to which they sacrifice to demons and not to God; for the thing that happens happens as it were for denial of God. [Label 1 Kor 10,22] Since it is written, God saying through Moses to them: 'they made me jealous with no-gods, they angered me with their idols', and the Corinthians were eating idol-sacrifices, because of this he says: 'or do we make the Lord jealous?' (instead of: do we provoke him?) 'are we stronger than he?' He showed by this that the Lord does not want us to eat idol-sacrifices. So do not, he says, want what the Lord does not want, as stronger and more understanding than he. [Second form, not printed again: Or do we move him to jealousy and provoke him? For it is said by Moses: they made me jealous with no-gods, they angered me with their idols. And he says these things since the Corinthians were eating idol-sacrifices.] [Label 1 Kor 10,25] Since it was likely that they, being over-exact, would no longer dare even to buy provisions for fear of hearing 'you bought idol-sacrifice', he consoles the fear. pass_b_english: …draw them over. People do not come to terms at all with those who agree with them in nothing, but they do with those who come part of the way to meet them.
On 1 Corinthians 9:23: Since the gospel too seems not to have made use of the law, I copied its way of managing things, handling matters as it wishes, so that in this very respect I may share in it.

On 1 Corinthians 9:24: He does not mean that one out of all of us is picked; otherwise people would have given up on themselves, seeing how hard success is. Clearly the picture is drawn with the nations he has just named in view. Everyone, he says, competes in this life as in a stadium: Jews by the law, Greeks by their error. But one alone is the word of truth, the one that wins and takes the prize. So run, so that you are not left behind with the rest.

On 1 Corinthians 9:25: What great thing is it, he says, if you abstain from meat for your brother's sake? The athlete must master himself in everything: in anger, in glory, and in all the rest. They do it to win a crown that perishes, but we a crown that does not. He did not say this idly. He was correcting those who, to fill their bellies, put on a show of philosophy and said that idol food is not idol food.

On 1 Corinthians 10:1–8: The inspired Paul brings forward the types from the old covenant and the shadows there that sketched in advance the truth to come, so as to sober the Corinthians by setting the ancients beside them. If, he says, those who were baptized into Moses, who was a type of Christ, in the cloud and the sea, who ate the manna, the spiritual food, and drank the spiritual drink from the rock, were struck down in the wilderness when they turned to drunkenness, fornication and idolatry, because they insulted the type and the shadow, what would those not suffer who sin against the truth itself?

On 1 Corinthians 10:9: Since they were saying, “For me there is no idol; I give thanks and eat,” this, he says, is putting the Lord to the test. When you do something Jesus did not command, as though you were trusting him, you are testing him rather than trusting him.

On 1 Corinthians 10:11: The coming of Christ has reached you, he says, and after it there will be no further commandment, no law, no prophets. By “the ends” he does not mean the last generation, at which the world will reach its completion, but the final way of life, the life in Christ, upon which the completion of the ages will arrive.
On 1 Corinthians 10:13: He did not pray that they should not be tested, since an untested man is unproven, but that they should be tested in a way they could bear.
The second catena form adds: From this he shows that those among them who believed had to endure some unpleasantness from their fellow citizens.
On 1 Corinthians 10:14: You see that everything he said before was being built up for this.
On 1 Corinthians 10:20: Do not look at their idols, which are nothing, but at the intent with which they sacrifice to demons and not to God. What is done there amounts to a denial of God.

On 1 Corinthians 10:22: It is written that God said to them through Moses, “They provoked me to jealousy with what is no god; they angered me with their idols” (Deuteronomy 32:21). The Corinthians were eating idol food. That is why he says, “Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy?” meaning “Are we stirring him to anger?” “Are we stronger than he?” By this he showed that the Lord does not want us to eat idol food. So do not want, he says, what the Lord does not want, as though you were stronger and wiser than he.

On 1 Corinthians 10:25: It was likely that, in their scruples, they would no longer dare even to buy food at market for fear of hearing, “You bought idol food.” So he eases that fear. By “conscience” he means not the conscience of the one who knows that an idol is nothing, but that of the one who has seen someone buying the…

choices.why: Context is abstaining from idol meat for the brother's sake (8:13).
Severianus glosses Paul's τὰ τέλη τῶν αἰώνων; quoted as Paul's word.

choices.english: meaning “Are we stirring him to anger?”
choices.why: ἀντὶ τοῦ marks a gloss on Paul's word.
Label lacks the verse; the words (they sacrifice to demons and not to God) are 10:20.

choices.why: Brief rule on doublets; 9:25 second form marked 257,col2; others are printed back to back.
